subject.title: Discord: make native command visibility follow account/channel routing

question: Which Discord command-visibility policy should OpenClaw support for multi-account setups?
rationale: Current source confirms execution-only auth, but syncing Discord command permissions, adding explicit reconcile/config controls, guild-scoped deployment, and namespacing have different Discord API, upgrade, and operator-control tradeoffs.

options.title: Derive visibility from routing
options.body: Use existing Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics, propagation behavior, and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Add explicit operator controls
options.body: Add a CLI or config-controlled reconciliation path so operators choose which accounts expose generic commands and when Discord permissions are rewritten.

options.title: Document manual setup
options.body: Keep OpenClaw execution auth unchanged and document manual Discord app permission setup as the supported multi-account visibility workflow.

recommendation.title: Derive visibility from routing
recommendation.body: Use existing Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics, propagation behavior, and cleanup behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source and recent history most directly route through vincentkoc on Discord command deploy and native command access behavior.
